method: Implemented the current MCP preview boundary repair after formal R14 recording, restricted to the four listed web files. Preserved exact before copies for the three preexisting files, added two failing-before regressions, reused unchanged mediaBytes/mediaMime, and reviewed scoped resource ownership and error fencing. A React-owned provider allows one current panel preview across all results/resources. Validation precedes object URL allocation; lifecycle cleanup revokes URLs, removes source attributes, stops audio and explicitly releases its resource. Read every changed implementation/test and ran only the listed exact targeted files, retaining both pre-repair failures and an intermediate StrictMode failure.
behavior: MCP images and audio require an explicit per-item preview/load action; the current MCP panel has one active preview across retained results and resources.
Strict Base64/encoded size, detected image/audio signature, declared-vs-detected MIME, positive bounded dimensions and the shared 40-million-pixel limit are checked before media source creation.
Rejected entries show a useful per-item error while sibling text, links, binary metadata, original result identity/body and raw JSON download remain usable.

Switching previews, result identity/content/item/type/MIME/bytes changes, result removal, scope/connection changes and unmount release the held preview; an old load error cannot close a replacement preview.

Audio uses preload=none without autoplay and is paused, detached from its source and reloaded empty on teardown. Image sources are removed on teardown. StrictMode ref reattachment restores only the already validated URL.

tests.detail: Two focused regressions failed against the original automatic img behavior.

failures.test: does not create image or audio sources until a separate preview action
failures.message: AssertionError: expected to be null

failures.test: rejects an oversized compact PNG header before creating a source and keeps sibling text visible
failures.message: AssertionError: expected to be null

tests.detail: 67 tests passed before explicit DOM media teardown and StrictMode coverage were added.
The new StrictMode regression failed because ref cleanup removed src and reattachment did not restore it; 68 other tests passed.

failures.test: keeps a live preview usable through StrictMode ref and effect checks and revokes once on unmount
failures.message: AssertionError: expected null to be 'blob:mcp-1' // Object.is equality

tests.detail: Restoring only the already validated object URL on ref reattachment fixed the regression.
Final exact files, including two type-only Blob assertions, passed 69 tests.

validations.detail: All changed files are UTF-8 without BOM and LF.
The first implementation apply_patch attempted delete/add of the same path in one patch and was rejected before any edit. Retried as an update patch; no source was partially replaced.

limitations: No full/aggregate test selection, build or typecheck was run by this agent; root owns final shared web noEmit/build and integration evidence.

No browser raster decoding, real large image, OOM, audio playback, external/network service, real MCP/provider/model, login, SSH or personal CODEX_HOME was used. JSDOM fixture tests use safe one-pixel images or small synthetic headers, mock Blob URLs and mock audio pause/load.
The shared parser validates signatures and dimension headers; browser-level corruption is handled by per-preview error cleanup, not claimed as a complete media-format validator.
Only this four-file repair is claimed here; root and the deployment reviewer independently crossreview integration. Changes by the separate attachment-repair agent are outside this report.
No capability coverage regeneration or formal round14 report edits were performed. The failing-before and intermediate failed runs are retained above and in their original ignored test reports.
